I would attribute around 85% of Nethereum’s Ethereum value to original work, or 80% if using the provided guide values.
 

 Nethereum is not primarily a fork or thin wrapper. It builds on Ethereum protocols, JSON-RPC endpoints, .NET, and standard cryptographic primitives, but its ecosystem value comes from a large amount of original implementation work: Ethereum data models, ABI/RLP/hex encoding, transaction signing, EIP-712 support, smart contract interaction, typed code generation, blockchain indexing, wallet/account tooling, Merkle Patricia trie verification, EVM simulation, account abstraction support, Unity/Blazor/MAUI integration, and broader .NET developer infrastructure.
 

 Some credit should be assigned to dependencies and upstream foundations such as Ethereum clients, Ethereum protocol specifications, .NET, and cryptographic libraries (like bouncycastle) However, those are mostly underlying platforms and standards. Nethereum’s distinctive contribution is implementing and maintaining a broad Ethereum development stack for the .NET ecosystem.
